extracted.intended_audience: artists, architects, and connoisseurs studying medieval Venetian church design and ornamentation
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of design and evaluative principles for Venetian medieval church architecture (especially apse/arch ornament): proportions, material choice, color/sculpture treatment, and ornament hierarchy as discussed in the Murano Duomo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic proportions in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The intervals between the shafts are exactly one fourth of the width of the nave; the distance between great piers is exactly three times the interval of the shafts. "So the four distances are accurately in arithmetical proportion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise numerical ratios in planning (example: interval of shafts 8'2", aisle 16'4", transept 24'6", nave 32'8"). Such measured arithmetical relations produce harmony and should be observed where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtle apse proportioning for harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: The seven external sides of the apse are arranged on a line less than a semicircle and in four magnitudes, the widest being the central one; these small deliberate variations reflect a 'true love of harmony.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportions that are not strictly repetitive but subtly varied (e.g., slight reductions of two inches on large widths) create a more graceful cadence than mechanical uniformity; such tiny, purposeful alterations should be employed to attain harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural buttressing by adapted shafts and arches
rubrics_metrics.description: The security of the apse's semi-dome is provided by a system of buttresses obtained entirely by adaptations of the Roman shaft and arch: niches flanked by pairs of shafts forming massy buttresses with an open gallery above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use architectural elements (shafts, niches, arches) both structurally and visually: arrange them so that their structural function (buttressing) also produces an ordered, pleasing exterior massing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material selection matched to function
rubrics_metrics.description: The building is mainly of yellow brick (used where strength required), with a deep red porous brick used chiefly for decoration, and several marbles used sparingly for ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose materials according to structural role and decorative effect: reserve stronger materials for load-bearing parts and use varied, more precious materials (marbles, colored bricks) for visual emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve color purity by limiting sculpture
rubrics_metrics.description: The purple capitals are left plain; the white are sculptured. Carving purple would mix grey shadow and 'adulterate the purity of the color' and draw attention from the color itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a material's color is a primary visual value, avoid deep carving that disrupts its surface and hue; reserve sculpture for paler stones where chiselling adds interest without spoiling color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation and symmetry of colored elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitals alternate purple and white in pairs (purple plain, white sculptured) so that two white meet in the centre; color alternation is used deliberately to create balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange colored elements in alternating sequences and mirrored groups so that color balance and focal points (e.g., two white meeting in centre) are achieved across the composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled variation in repeated ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: The trefoil motif is repeated five or six hundred times, but 'hardly ever twice of the same size'—a principle modelled on nature: the same leaf repeated but never identically sized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat motifs with deliberate, measured variation in scale and proportion to avoid monotony and to imitate organic variety; ensure the variations are purposeful and measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust ornament relief to viewing distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Carvings are thrown out in low and flat relief with intermediate spaces cut only about a quarter inch, which 'insures the visibility of all its parts at the necessary distance (17 or 18 feet)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design relief depth and detail scale with expected viewing distance: use shallower relief and simpler forms when viewers are farther away so details read clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dark accents to emphasize centers
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of black and white marble is used to emphasize the centre of the chain, 'exactly as a painter would use a dark touch for a similar purpose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ strong tonal or color accents strategically to mark focal points or centers within a repetitive decorative band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match carving detail to material quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Carving is made finer where variegated marbles are used and bolder where coarse brick and dark stone occur, so the level of chiselling corresponds to the material's visual fineness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust intricacy of ornament to the fineness and visual character of the material: delicate chiselling on fine veined marbles, bolder motifs on coarse materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric adjustment to subordinate decorative bands
rubrics_metrics.description: The upper band of triangles is made about two inches higher and more acute to look lighter and be subordinated to the richly decorated lower series; elsewhere bases are narrowed to change emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subtle geometric changes (height, acuity, base width) to create visual hierarchy between adjacent decorative bands so one reads as subordinate to the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight structural irregularities as deliberate features
rubrics_metrics.description: When awkward junctions or shape-difficulties occur, the medieval builder 'directed the eye to the difficulty' and made the inserted awkward stone conspicuous by using contrasting colors (e.g., grey and green) so the difficulty becomes a celebrated feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hide awkward structural conditions; instead, treat them as opportunities for compositional emphasis using contrast, thus turning defects into intentional focal points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate multiple decorative courses into a harmonious whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Two bands of triangles are separated by a string-course, but differences (height, width) are deliberately managed—so 'the two courses, instead of repeating, unite with each other, and become a harmonious whole.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing successive decorative layers, plan their proportions and relations so they complement rather than merely repeat; use adjustments to ensure overall unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inlaid geometric units (triangles) to form ornamental chains
rubrics_metrics.description: A band composed of close-set triangles of various marbles and bricks is described as 'thrown, like a necklace of precious stones, round the apse' with groups and specific sequences to answer each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose continuous inlaid patterns from a limited set of geometric units and material types, arranging groups and sequences to create rhythm, emphasis, and bilateral response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create hierarchical richness by material selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The lower (central) series is made more precious—no brick and three kinds of variegated marble—whereas the flanking series contains brick and fewer marbles, so the center reads as richer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a material hierarchy to mark importance: reserve the finest materials and greatest variety for central or focal bands, using simpler materials for adjacent or subordinate zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal incised ornament to preserve veined surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Purple marbles in the archivolt are 'touched with sculpture' by fine incision so as to 'destroy their colored surface as little as possible'; ornament is merely outlined rather than deeply carved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On richly veined or colored stones, prefer shallow incised ornament to full relief carving so that the stone's surface and color pattern remain visually dominant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of measured architectural members
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed dimensions are given for shafts, piers, and apse geometry (shaft circumference, pier widths, distances to apse curve); such exact measures inform proportion and design choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and design with precise measurements for columns, piers, and modular intervals—the exactness of these dimensions underpins the proportional system and the resulting aesthetic harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design correspondences even if not simultaneously visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups on each side of the apse 'answer each other' and balance one another though no one could see both sides at the same time; the balance is intentional across the whole composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan bilateral or complementary correspondences across a structure to achieve compositional balance, even when full simultaneity of view is impossible for a single observer.
